source.text: Ἤκουσεν Ἰησοῦς ὅτι ἐξέβαλον αὐτὸν ἔξω, καὶ εὑρὼν αὐτὸν εἶπεν· Σὺ πιστεύεις εἰς τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου;

records.literal_gloss: Heard Jesus that they had thrown him out, and having found him he said, "You, do you believe in the Son of the man?"

en.L: Jesus heard that they had thrown him out, and having found him, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Do you believe in the Son of Man?"
en.B: Jesus heard that they had thrown the man out, and when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} found him, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Do you believe in the Son of Man?"
en.R: Jesus heard that the leaders had thrown the man out. So Jesus went and found him and asked, "Do you believe in the Son of Man?"

es.L: Oyó Jesús que lo habían echado fuera, y hallándolo, le dijo: «¿Tú crees en el Hijo del Hombre?».
es.B: Jesús oyó que habían echado fuera al hombre, y cuando lo encontró, le dijo: «¿Crees tú en el Hijo del Hombre?».
es.R: Jesús oyó que los dirigentes habían echado fuera al hombre. Entonces fue a buscarlo y le preguntó: «¿Crees en el Hijo del Hombre?».

sw.L: Yesu alisikia kwamba wamemtupa nje, na alipomkuta, akasema, "Je, wewe unamwamini Mwana wa Adamu?"
sw.B: Yesu alisikia kwamba wamemtupa mtu yule nje, na alipomkuta, akamwambia, "Je, unamwamini Mwana wa Adamu?"
sw.R: Yesu alisikia kwamba viongozi walikuwa wamemfukuza mtu yule. Basi Yesu alikwenda akamtafuta, akamwuliza, "Je, unamwamini Mwana wa Adamu?"

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu nghe rằng họ đã đuổi anh ta ra ngoài, và khi gặp anh ta, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói: "Anh có tin vào Con Người không?"
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu nghe tin họ đã đuổi anh ta ra, nên khi gặp anh ta, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hỏi: "Anh có tin vào Con Người không?"
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nghe tin các nhà lãnh đạo đã đuổi người ấy ra. Vậy Ngài đi tìm anh ta và hỏi: "Anh có tin vào Con Người không?"

decisions.choice: the Son of Man (SBLGNT)
alternatives: the Son of God (many later manuscripts)
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "the Son of God". The oldest witnesses, among them two early papyri, Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus, read "the Son of Man", the title Jesus uses of himself throughout John. A change from the unusual question about the Son of Man to the more familiar confession of the Son of God is easier to explain than the reverse. A footnote gives the other reading. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: they threw him out: the leaders drove him from their presence, and with it, in the light of 9:22, from the synagogue community
alternatives: they only sent him out of the room
a formal sentence of expulsion pronounced on the spot
decisions.reason: The words repeat the end of verse 34. They at least mean that the Pharisees put him out of their presence in contempt. John has already said that the authorities had agreed to put out of the synagogue anyone who confessed Jesus as the Christ (9:22), so the reader is meant to see the man suffering what his parents feared. John does not describe any formal procedure.

decisions.choice: Jesus seeks the man out
decisions.reason: As with the man healed at the pool (5:14), it is Jesus who finds the man after the healing. The one the authorities have thrown out is sought and received by Jesus (compare 6:37; 10:3-4).

decisions.choice: you, do you believe: the pronoun is emphatic
alternatives: a plain question with no stress on the person
decisions.reason: The Greek states "you" where the verb alone would do. It sets the man over against the Pharisees who have refused to believe: whatever they think, does he believe?

decisions.choice: the Son of Man: Jesus's title for himself
alternatives: a general expression for a human being
decisions.reason: In John the Son of Man is the one who comes down from heaven and is lifted up (1:51; 3:13-14; 8:28), and the one to whom the Father has given authority to judge (5:27). That last point prepares for verse 39. The title draws on Daniel 7:13-14. The man does not yet know that Jesus is speaking of himself (verse 36).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}
decisions.reason: Every pronoun for Christ uses the deity_pronoun setting, including the pronouns for the Son of Man in verse 36, since the one asked about is Jesus (as with the coming Messiah at 4:25 and 7:27), and "you" when people speak to him. At the start of a sentence "He" is written plain. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: the leaders; So Jesus went and found him
decisions.reason: Readable names who "they" were, the leaders who questioned the man in verses 13-34, and makes plain that Jesus went looking for him (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: tú, no setting
decisions.reason: The emphatic "tú" (meaning decision m4) is the man and has no setting.

decisions.choice: los dirigentes; fue a buscarlo
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable names who "they" were and that Jesus sought the man out (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: Jesus calls the man "anh"
decisions.reason: An adult of unknown age; "anh" is the plain respectful form, as the neighbours and the leaders also use. "Con" would make Jesus his elder or teacher before the man has come to faith.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} for Jesus in the narrative; plain "Ngài" at the start of a sentence
decisions.reason: Only the capital letter changes with the setting.

source.text: ἀπεκρίθη ἐκεῖνος καὶ εἶπεν· Καὶ τίς ἐστιν, κύριε, ἵνα πιστεύσω εἰς αὐτόν;

records.literal_gloss: Answered that [one] and said, "And who is he, sir, that I may believe in him?"

en.L: That [man] answered and said, "And who is {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, Sir, so that I may believe in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}?"
en.B: The man answered, "Who is {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, Sir? Tell me, so that I may believe in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."
en.R: The man answered, "Sir, who is {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}? I want to believe in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

es.L: Respondió aquel y dijo: «¿Y quién es, Señor, para que crea en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}?».
es.B: El hombre respondió: «¿Quién es, Señor? Dímelo, para que crea en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}».
es.R: El hombre respondió: «Señor, ¿quién es? Quiero creer en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}».

sw.L: Yule akajibu, akasema, "Naye ni nani, bwana, ili nipate kumwamini?"
sw.B: Mtu yule akajibu, "Ni nani huyo, bwana? Niambie, ili nipate kumwamini."
sw.R: Mtu yule akajibu, "Ni nani huyo, bwana? Nataka kumwamini."

vi.L: Người ấy đáp và nói: "Vậy Đấng ấy là ai, thưa ông, để tôi tin vào Đấng ấy?"
vi.B: Anh ta đáp: "Thưa ông, Đấng ấy là ai? Xin cho tôi biết để tôi tin vào Đấng ấy."
vi.R: Người ấy trả lời: "Thưa ông, Đấng ấy là ai? Tôi muốn tin vào Đấng ấy."

decisions.choice: Sir: a respectful address
alternatives: Lord, a confession of who Jesus is
decisions.reason: The word is the polite form used to anyone of standing, as the Samaritan woman uses it (4:11, 15, 19). The man already holds Jesus to be a prophet (9:17) and sent from God (9:33), but he does not yet know who the Son of Man is, or that he is speaking to him. In verse 38, once he believes, the same word carries the full sense of "Lord". A footnote gives "Lord".

decisions.choice: and who is he, so that I may believe: an eager question; he is ready to believe once he knows
decisions.reason: The opening "and" gives the question urgency, and the clause of purpose shows why he asks: he wants to know whom to believe in. He does not refuse the question; he asks to be shown.

decisions.choice: he and him: the Son of Man, who is Jesus himself
decisions.reason: The man asks about a third person, but the reader knows the answer, and verse 37 gives it: the one he is speaking to.

decisions.choice: Sir
decisions.reason: Shows the polite address (meaning decision m1), so that the change to "Lord" in verse 38 can be seen.

decisions.choice: Tell me, so that
decisions.reason: Balanced breaks the question in two and supplies "Tell me", which the clause of purpose implies (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: Señor
decisions.reason: Here "señor" is the polite address (meaning decision m1); in 9:38 the same word becomes "Lord" as the man believes. English shows the change with "Sir" and "Lord"; Spanish keeps one word, as the Greek does, and the footnote points it out.

decisions.choice: Dímelo
decisions.reason: As in English: supplies what the clause of purpose implies (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: bwana here; Bwana in verse 38
decisions.reason: The man uses the same Greek word twice. In verse 36 he does not yet know who Jesus is, so it is a polite "sir", placed inside the sentence to stay lowercase, as in John 4 and 5. In verse 38, after he believes, it is "Bwana" (Lord), as the meaning notes and the book-wide choice for John have it.

decisions.choice: "thưa ông" for kyrie
decisions.reason: He does not yet know who is speaking to him, so he says what one says to a respected stranger; in 9:38 the same Greek word becomes "Lạy Chúa".

decisions.choice: "Đấng ấy" for the Son of Man, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The man speaks with reverence of the Son of Man without knowing he is Jesus; "Đấng ấy" says that in Vietnamese and is a noun phrase that the setting does not change. Jesus answers with the same words in 9:37.

source.text: εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Καὶ ἑώρακας αὐτὸν καὶ ὁ λαλῶν μετὰ σοῦ ἐκεῖνός ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: Said to him the Jesus, "Both you have seen him, and the [one] speaking with you, that [one] is."

en.L: Jesus said to him, "You have both seen {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and the one speaking with you is that [one]."
en.B: Jesus said to him, "You have seen {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the one who is speaking with you."
en.R: Jesus said to him, "You have seen {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with your own eyes. He is the one talking with you right now."

es.L: Le dijo Jesús: «Lo has visto, y el que habla contigo, ese es».
es.B: Jesús le dijo: «Ya lo has visto; es el que está hablando contigo».
es.R: Jesús le dijo: «Lo has visto con tus propios ojos. Es el que está hablando contigo ahora mismo».

sw.L: Yesu akamwambia, "Umemwona, na yeye anayesema nawe ndiye."
sw.R: Yesu akamwambia, "Umemwona kwa macho yako mwenyewe. Yeye ndiye anayezungumza nawe sasa hivi."

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu nói với anh ta: "Anh đã thấy Đấng ấy rồi, và chính người đang nói với anh là Đấng ấy."
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu nói với anh ta: "Anh đã thấy Đấng ấy; chính Đấng ấy đang nói chuyện với anh đây."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói với anh ta: "Anh đã thấy Đấng ấy tận mắt. Chính Đấng ấy đang nói chuyện với anh đây."

decisions.choice: you have seen him: the man who was blind has now seen the Son of Man
alternatives: only a figure of speech for knowing him
decisions.reason: The man was sent away to wash before he could see (9:7), so this is the first time he has seen Jesus. The perfect tense stresses that the seeing has happened and stands. The words also prepare for verse 39: his eyes see, and now he is coming to see who Jesus is.

decisions.choice: the one speaking with you is he: Jesus reveals himself as he did to the Samaritan woman
decisions.reason: The words echo 4:26, where Jesus tells the woman that the Messiah she expects is the one speaking with her. In both places Jesus makes himself known to someone who has asked.

decisions.choice: both ... and: two ways of meeting him, seeing and hearing
alternatives: the first "and" as a mere connective
decisions.reason: The paired "and ... and" joins the two clauses: he has seen him, and he is hearing him now. The emphatic "that one" points from the Son of Man asked about to the speaker.

decisions.choice: is that [one]
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek pointing word "that one" at the end; Balanced turns it round to the natural order.

decisions.choice: with your own eyes; right now
decisions.reason: Readable brings out that the man is now seeing with eyes that were blind (meaning decision m1), and that the speaker is present before him.

decisions.choice: ese es (L)
decisions.reason: As in English: Literal keeps the pointing word at the end; it echoes 4:26 (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: con tus propios ojos; ahora mismo
decisions.reason: As in English: brings out that the man now sees with eyes that were blind (meaning decision m1).

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἔφη· Πιστεύω, κύριε· καὶ προσεκύνησεν αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: He then said, "I believe, lord"; and he worshiped him.

en.L: And he said, "I believe, Lord." And he worshiped {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: He said, "I believe, Lord." And he worshiped {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: The man said, "I believe, Lord!" And he bowed down and worshiped {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y él dijo: «Creo, Señor». Y lo adoró.
es.B: Él dijo: «Creo, Señor». Y lo adoró.
es.R: El hombre dijo: «¡Creo, Señor!». Y se inclinó y lo adoró.

sw.R: Mtu yule akasema, "Naamini, Bwana!" Akainama akamwabudu.

vi.L: Anh ta nói: "Con tin, lạy Chúa." Rồi anh ta thờ lạy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Anh ta nói: "Lạy Chúa, con tin!" Và anh ta thờ lạy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Người ấy nói: "Lạy Chúa, con tin!" Rồi anh ta quỳ xuống thờ lạy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

decisions.choice: the words are part of the text (SBLGNT)
alternatives: the words "He said, 'I believe, Lord,' and he worshiped him. And Jesus said" (verses 38 and the start of 39) are missing
decisions.reason: A few early witnesses, among them an early papyrus (P75), the first hand of Codex Sinaiticus and Codex W, lack this verse and the opening words of verse 39, so that Jesus's words in verse 39 follow straight on from verse 37. Almost all other manuscripts have them, and the SBLGNT prints them. A footnote notes the omission. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Lord: now an address of faith
alternatives: Sir, a polite address as in verse 36
decisions.reason: It is the same word the man used in verse 36, but he now says it as he confesses his faith in the Son of Man. Those who have come to believe call Jesus "Lord" (6:68; 11:27; 20:28). The word is the same; what has changed is the man who says it.

decisions.choice: worshiped: bowed down before him in worship
alternatives: knelt before him in respect, as before an honored human
decisions.reason: The verb means to bow down before someone, and it can be used of homage to a human superior (Matthew 18:26). In John, though, it is used only of worshiping God (4:20-24; 12:20), and here it follows a confession of faith in the Son of Man. A footnote gives "knelt before him".

decisions.choice: I believe: the end of the man's journey from blindness to faith
decisions.reason: Step by step the man has spoken of "the man called Jesus" (9:11), "a prophet" (9:17) and one "from God" (9:33); now he believes and worships. The Pharisees have moved the other way, from questions to rejection, as verses 39-41 bring out.

decisions.choice: Lord
decisions.reason: The address changes from "Sir" (verse 36) to "Lord" because the man now believes (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: bowed down and worshiped
decisions.reason: Readable shows the bodily act the verb describes as well as its sense (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: Señor: now "Lord"
decisions.reason: The same word as in 9:36, now spoken in faith (meaning decision m2); see the note there.

decisions.choice: se inclinó y lo adoró
decisions.reason: As in English: shows the bodily act as well as its sense (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: "Lạy Chúa" and "con", where 9:36 had "thưa ông" and "tôi"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese shows his new faith in the forms of address: he calls Jesus "Chúa" as believers do and speaks of himself as "con", as the style guide has believers do.

source.text: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Εἰς κρίμα ἐγὼ εἰς τὸν κόσμον τοῦτον ἦλθον, ἵνα οἱ μὴ βλέποντες βλέπωσιν καὶ οἱ βλέποντες τυφλοὶ γένωνται.

records.literal_gloss: And said the Jesus, "For judgment I into the world this came, that the [ones] not seeing may see and the [ones] seeing blind may become."

en.L: And Jesus said, "For judgment I came into this world, so that the [ones] not seeing may see, and the [ones] seeing may become blind."
en.B: Jesus said, "I came into this world to bring judgment, so that those who cannot see will see, and those who see will become blind."
en.R: Jesus said, "I came into this world to bring judgment. I came so that people who are blind can see, and people who think they can see will become blind."

es.L: Y dijo Jesús: «Para juicio vine yo a este mundo, para que los que no ven vean, y los que ven se vuelvan ciegos».
es.B: Jesús dijo: «Vine a este mundo para hacer juicio, para que los que no ven vean, y los que ven se queden ciegos».
es.R: Jesús dijo: «Vine a este mundo para traer juicio. Vine para que los ciegos puedan ver, y para que los que creen que ven se vuelvan ciegos».

sw.L: Na Yesu akasema, "Kwa ajili ya hukumu mimi nilikuja katika ulimwengu huu, ili wale wasioona waone, na wale wanaoona wageuke kuwa vipofu."
sw.B: Yesu akasema, "Nilikuja katika ulimwengu huu kuleta hukumu, ili wale wasioweza kuona waone, na wale wanaoona wawe vipofu."
sw.R: Yesu akasema, "Nilikuja katika ulimwengu huu kuleta hukumu. Nilikuja ili watu walio vipofu waweze kuona, na watu wanaodhani wanaona wawe vipofu."

vi.L: Và Đức Giê-xu nói: "Vì sự phán xét, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã đến thế gian này, để những người không thấy thì được thấy, và những người thấy thì trở nên mù."
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu nói: "Ta đã đến thế gian này để thi hành sự phán xét, để những người không thấy sẽ thấy được, còn những người thấy được lại trở nên mù."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói: "Ta đến thế gian này để mang lại sự phán xét. Ta đến để những người mù được thấy, còn những người tưởng mình thấy được sẽ trở nên mù."

decisions.choice: judgment: a verdict that separates people, brought about by his coming
alternatives: condemnation as the aim of his coming
the act of judging in a court
decisions.reason: The word is the result of judging, a verdict. Here it is the division that Jesus's coming brings about between those who come to see and those who refuse to.

decisions.choice: his coming brings judgment, though he did not come to condemn
decisions.reason: In 3:17 God did not send the Son to judge the world but to save it, and in 12:47 Jesus says the same. Yet the Father has given all judgment to the Son (5:22, 27), and 3:19 explains how both are true: the light has come, and people's response to it is itself the judgment. Here the man who was blind has come to the light, and the Pharisees have turned from it.

decisions.choice: so that: the purpose of his coming, which is also its outcome
decisions.reason: The conjunction normally states a purpose. Jesus came to give sight; that those who claim to see become blind is the other side of the same coming, as light that shows the way also exposes those who turn away from it (3:19-21).

decisions.choice: giving sight to the blind and blinding those who see: echoes of Isaiah
decisions.reason: Isaiah promises that the eyes of the blind will be opened (Isaiah 29:18; 35:5; 42:7), and speaks of a people who see but do not perceive, whose eyes are shut (Isaiah 6:9-10, quoted in John 12:40; compare 42:18-19).

decisions.choice: seeing and blindness in two senses: the body's eyes and understanding of God
decisions.reason: The whole chapter turns on this. The man born blind receives his sight and comes to see who Jesus is; the Pharisees, who can see and claim to know (9:24, 29), become blind to him. Those who "see" are those who think they see (verse 41).

decisions.choice: to bring judgment
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly what "for judgment" means (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: people who think they can see
decisions.reason: Readable makes explicit that the seeing is claimed, as Jesus says in verse 41 (meaning decision m5).

decisions.choice: para hacer juicio (B); para traer juicio (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: says what "for judgment" means (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: los que creen que ven
decisions.reason: As in English: the seeing is claimed (meaning decision m5).

source.text: ἤκουσαν ἐκ τῶν Φαρισαίων ταῦτα οἱ μετ’ αὐτοῦ ὄντες, καὶ εἶπον αὐτῷ· Μὴ καὶ ἡμεῖς τυφλοί ἐσμεν;

records.literal_gloss: Heard [some] of the Pharisees these things, the [ones] with him being, and they said to him, "Not also we blind are?"

en.L: [Some] of the Pharisees who were with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} heard these things, and they said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "We are not blind too, are we?"
en.B: Some of the Pharisees who were with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} heard this and said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "You do not mean that we are blind too, do you?"
en.R: Some of the Pharisees who were there with Jesus heard this. They said to Jesus, "You are not saying that we are blind too, are you?"

es.L: [Algunos] de los fariseos que estaban con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} oyeron estas cosas y le dijeron: «¿Acaso también nosotros somos ciegos?».
es.B: Algunos de los fariseos que estaban con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} oyeron esto y le dijeron: «¿No estarás diciendo que también nosotros somos ciegos?».
es.R: Algunos de los fariseos que estaban allí con Jesús oyeron esto. Le dijeron: «No estás diciendo que nosotros también somos ciegos, ¿verdad?».

sw.L: [Baadhi] ya Mafarisayo waliokuwa pamoja naye walisikia mambo haya, wakamwambia, "Je, sisi nasi ni vipofu?"
sw.B: Baadhi ya Mafarisayo waliokuwa pamoja naye walisikia hayo, wakamwambia, "Hakika humaanishi kwamba sisi nasi ni vipofu?"
sw.R: Baadhi ya Mafarisayo waliokuwa pale pamoja na Yesu walisikia hayo. Wakamwambia Yesu, "Husemi kwamba sisi nasi ni vipofu, sivyo?"

vi.L: [Một số] người Pha-ri-si đang ở với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nghe những điều này, thì nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Chẳng lẽ chúng tôi cũng mù sao?"
vi.B: Mấy người Pha-ri-si đang ở với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nghe vậy thì nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Ông không có ý nói chúng tôi cũng mù chứ?"
vi.R: Mấy người Pha-ri-si đang ở đó với Đức Giê-xu nghe vậy. Họ nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Ông không nói là chúng tôi cũng mù đấy chứ?"

decisions.choice: a question that expects the answer no
decisions.reason: The question begins with a particle that looks for a denial. The Pharisees do not ask whether they are blind; they object that Jesus cannot be saying so.

decisions.choice: we too: we as well as others he calls blind
decisions.reason: The stress falls on "we": they assume that blindness belongs to people like the man they have just called a sinner (9:34), not to teachers of the Law.

decisions.choice: who were with him: who were present with Jesus at the time
decisions.reason: The phrase means only that they were there. These Pharisees were not his disciples (9:28); they heard what he said to the man.

decisions.choice: You do not mean that ... do you? (B); You are not saying that ... are you? (R)
decisions.reason: The English puts the expected "no" into the question (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: [Some] of
decisions.reason: The Greek says "of the Pharisees", meaning some of them; Literal brackets the supplied word.

decisions.choice: ¿Acaso ...? (L); ¿No estarás diciendo ...? (B); ..., ¿verdad? (R)
decisions.reason: Puts the expected "no" into the question (meaning decision m1).

source.text: εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Εἰ τυφλοὶ ἦτε, οὐκ ἂν εἴχετε ἁμαρτίαν· νῦν δὲ λέγετε ὅτι Βλέπομεν· ἡ ἁμαρτία ὑμῶν μένει.

records.literal_gloss: Said to them the Jesus, "If blind you were, not would you have sin; now but you say that, 'We see'; the sin of you remains."

en.L: Jesus said to them, "If you were blind, you would not have sin; but now you say, 'We see'; your sin remains."
en.B: Jesus said to them, "If you were blind, you would have no sin. But you say, 'We can see,' so your sin remains."
en.R: Jesus said to them, "If you were blind, you would not be guilty of sin. But you say, 'We can see.' So your sin remains."

es.L: Jesús les dijo: «Si {{plural_you:fueran|fuerais}} ciegos, no {{plural_you:tendrían|tendríais}} pecado; pero ahora {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}: “Vemos”; {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} pecado permanece».
es.B: Jesús les dijo: «Si {{plural_you:fueran|fuerais}} ciegos, no {{plural_you:tendrían|tendríais}} pecado. Pero {{plural_you:ustedes dicen|vosotros decís}}: “Vemos”, así que {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} pecado permanece».
es.R: Jesús les dijo: «Si {{plural_you:fueran|fuerais}} ciegos, no {{plural_you:serían culpables|seríais culpables}} de pecado. Pero {{plural_you:ustedes dicen|vosotros decís}}: “Podemos ver”. Así que {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} pecado permanece».

sw.L: Yesu akawaambia, "Kama mngekuwa vipofu, dhambi hamngekuwa nayo; lakini sasa mnasema, 'Tunaona'; dhambi yenu inakaa juu yenu."
sw.B: Yesu akawaambia, "Kama mngekuwa vipofu, hamngekuwa na dhambi. Lakini mnasema, 'Tunaweza kuona,' kwa hiyo dhambi yenu inakaa juu yenu."
sw.R: Yesu akawaambia, "Kama mngekuwa vipofu, hamngekuwa na hatia ya dhambi. Lakini mnasema, 'Tunaweza kuona.' Kwa hiyo dhambi yenu inakaa juu yenu."

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Nếu các người mù, thì các người đã chẳng có tội; nhưng bây giờ các người nói: 'Chúng tôi thấy'; tội các người vẫn còn."
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Nếu các người mù, thì các người đã không có tội. Nhưng các người nói: 'Chúng tôi thấy được,' nên tội các người vẫn còn."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Nếu các người mù, thì các người không mắc tội. Nhưng các người nói: 'Chúng tôi thấy được.' Vì vậy tội các người vẫn còn."

decisions.choice: a condition contrary to fact: they are not blind in the way that would excuse them
decisions.reason: The form of the sentence assumes that the condition is not true. They are not people who cannot see; they claim to see.

decisions.choice: to have sin: to be guilty of sin
decisions.reason: John uses the phrase for guilt that a person must answer for (15:22, 24; 19:11). Those who truly could not see would not be held guilty for failing to see.

decisions.choice: their sin is claiming sight while refusing it
alternatives: they are guilty because of what they know
decisions.reason: The Pharisees claim to know (9:24, 29) and yet refuse the light that has come (3:19-20). Their claim to see leaves them no excuse; in the same way Jesus says that those who do not believe will die in their sins (8:24).

decisions.choice: remains: stays on them and is not taken away
decisions.reason: The verb is the one John uses for what lasts. As God's wrath remains on whoever refuses to obey the Son (3:36), so their sin remains, because they turn from the one who takes away the sin of the world (1:29).

decisions.choice: would have no sin (B); would not be guilty of sin (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what having sin means here (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: so
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply "so" to show that their sin remains because of their claim, which the Greek implies by setting the two clauses side by side.

decisions.choice: permanece
decisions.reason: John's weighty "remain", as in 3:36, where God's wrath remains (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: no serían culpables de pecado
decisions.reason: As in English: says what having sin means here (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: inakaa juu yenu
decisions.reason: The verb is "remain", and Swahili uses "kukaa" as in 3:36, where God's wrath remains on the one who disobeys. "Juu yenu" (on you) says that the sin stays on them, as the meaning note puts it.

decisions.choice: "vẫn còn" for remains
decisions.reason: An ordinary sense of meno, so the natural word rather than the key-term "ở lại".
